key_insight: The paper shows that training large language models on step-by-step reaction mechanism reasoning can improve chemical intelligence beyond coarse product prediction.
engineering_relevance: Mechanism-aware LLMs could make reaction prediction and retrosynthesis more physically consistent and more useful for computational chemistry workflows.
method: Built a large-scale dataset of reaction mechanisms for reasoning-oriented training.
Created FukuyamaBench from Fukuyama's Advanced Organic Reaction Mechanism book to test hierarchical mechanism reasoning.
Fine-tuned Qwen3-30B-A3B for mechanism-aware chemical reasoning.
evidence_signal: On FukuyamaBench Set A, the fine-tuned Qwen3-30B-A3B achieved 8.3% exact pathway match, outperforming the specialized FlowER model at 5.1%.
watch_item: Exact pathway matching remains very low, so real-world robustness and generalization across broader chemical spaces still need careful validation.
paper_title: Learning Mechanistic Reasoning for Chemical Reactions with Large Language Models
